<reason>CON won the financing clash. PRO repeated idle seats cost almost nothing to serve; CON separated serving cost from buying cost - leagues and dramas must be paid upfront - and showed costless exit creates adverse selection where peak-hoppers shrink the aggregate that pays a fixed rights bill, raising prices for steady households. PRO's stay-put discount answer was neutralized by that logic, and its rare-pause vs common-pause defense conceded the price must move if many pause. A answered pressure directly with transit-pass commitment pricing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's Rebuttal 1 to Rebuttal 2 chain on the idle-seat fallacy and the loses-either-way dilemma - rare pause is pointless machinery, common pause refunds the off-season revenue that funds risk - most damaged PRO's live route that flexibility is costless insurance.</best_rebuttal>
